Messages.Author: Jozxyqk
Messages.Body:
OK, I lied. Here's another question: :)

Enchant Kindred allows you to put blood onto younger
uncontrolled vampires.
If the capacity is met, does that vampire still wait
until the end of the Influence phase to come out?

If the vamp is only one below capacity, does the second
blood still go onto it, and then flow back into the Blood
Pool after revealing, or does it immediately 'cap'?
Can you deliberately "overflow" a vampire with multiple
Enchant Kindred cards from multiple sources?
(To scare your opponents into thinking that your
one-capacity Caitiff is a 6 or 7 capacity badass, or
something else equally meta-useful)

Messages.Author: Gomi no Sensei
Messages.Body:
In article <%Spb6.12389$t3.26...@typhoon.ne.mediaone.net>,

Jozxyqk <jfeu...@eecs.tufts.edu> wrote:
>OK, I lied. Here's another question: :)

Heh.

>Enchant Kindred allows you to put blood onto younger
>uncontrolled vampires.
>If the capacity is met, does that vampire still wait
>until the end of the Influence phase to come out?

Yep. No introducing new vampires in the middle of your
minion phase.

>If the vamp is only one below capacity, does the second
>blood still go onto it, and then flow back into the Blood
>Pool after revealing, or does it immediately 'cap'?

A full vampire must move into the controlled area at the end
of the influence phase; that's compulsory. A vampire with
blood in excess of capacity loses that blood immediately
to the Blood Bank.

Therefore, if Smudge is Enchanted twice, at the end of the
influence phase he moves into the controlled area with 4
blood, 3 of which immediately drain off to the blood bank.

Since Smudge won't leave the uncontrolled region until
the _end_ of the influence phase, however, you can spend
transfers to move blood off him to your pool before that
happens. Moving blood off a vampire and into the pool
costs 2 transfers rather than one, so barring an Info
Highway, you're only getting 2 blood off of him.

>Can you deliberately "overflow" a vampire with multiple
>Enchant Kindred cards from multiple sources?

Sure, with the caveat that once a vampire is at or over
capacity, he must move into the controlled region at
the end of your next influence phase.

>(To scare your opponents into thinking that your
>one-capacity Caitiff is a 6 or 7 capacity badass, or
>something else equally meta-useful)

Since typically they won't have a chance to take
any actions or play any action cards between the
time you overfill the Caitiff and the time he's
revealed, this is a tactic of limited use. Plus,
since you can only Enchant a younger vampire, it'll
be a pretty obvious bluff unless all the Enchanters
are 7 or 8 capacity. The first time Gideon Fontaine
Enchants, they'll know the vampire is 2 capacity
or smaller.

gomi

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Jozxyqk <jfeu...@eecs.tufts.edu> wrote:
> Enchant Kindred allows you to put blood onto younger
> uncontrolled vampires.
> If the capacity is met, does that vampire still wait
> until the end of the Influence phase to come out?

Yes.

> If the vamp is only one below capacity, does the second
> blood still go onto it, and then flow back into the Blood
> Pool after revealing, or does it immediately 'cap'?

It stays. Blood only "drains off" to the blood bank
once the vampire becomes controlled.

> Can you deliberately "overflow" a vampire with multiple
> Enchant Kindred cards from multiple sources?

Yes. But it will become controlled at the end of your
influence phase (unless you transfer enough blood off
of it before then).

Messages.Author: The Lasombra
Messages.Body:
In article <%Spb6.12389$t3.26...@typhoon.ne.mediaone.net>,
Jozxyqk <jfeu...@eecs.tufts.edu> wrote:

> OK, I lied. Here's another question: :)
>
> Enchant Kindred allows you to put blood onto younger
> uncontrolled vampires.
> If the capacity is met, does that vampire still wait
> until the end of the Influence phase to come out?

Yes, it has to wait until the end of your Influence phase to come out.

> If the vamp is only one below capacity, does the second
> blood still go onto it, and then flow back into the Blood
> Pool after revealing, or does it immediately 'cap'?

It can have more blood on it than its capacity, which you
may transfer off during your influence phase, before it comes
into play.

> Can you deliberately "overflow" a vampire with multiple
> Enchant Kindred cards from multiple sources?

Yes.

Messages.Author: Halcyan 2
Messages.Body:
>> If the vamp is only one below capacity, does the second
>> blood still go onto it, and then flow back into the Blood
>> Pool after revealing, or does it immediately 'cap'?
>
>It stays. Blood only "drains off" to the blood bank
>once the vampire becomes controlled.

In the case that cards affecting capacity (skill cards, some Praxis', etc.) are
on the vampire, do these take into effect before or after the draining of
blood?

For example: I have what is normally a 5-cap vampire with two skill cards
(making him a 7-cap in play). But he gets Banished and so he's only treated as
a 5-cap while I have to re-influence him. If I put 7 blood on him and he then
enters play, will the blood drain off before the capacity-enhancing effect of
the skill cards kicks in? Thanks!

Halcyan 2
